statement: Routing scoped coding work down a ladder of deterministic tools and local models returns more accepted work per unit of expensive-token spend than having the calling agent do that work itself.
de_risk_milestone: v1 minimal telemetry over real tasks on the author's own repositories: accepted-and-merged work per expensive token, compared against the same contracts executed on the API tier. If offload does not win — because escalation after local failure costs more than starting high, or because deterministic exploration cannot bound planning spend — the product's premise is wrong and the ladder should collapse to the tiers that do win.

citations.supports_because: Establishes the necessary condition, not the claim itself: a 3B model reaches 80.5% and a 7B 82.9% on scoped function synthesis, so a meaningful share of grunt work is within local reach at zero token cost. It says nothing about whether the surrounding orchestration is cheaper than not orchestrating.

_note: This is the product's reason to exist and it is deliberately registered as unmeasured. local-ai built the execution pipeline to answer it and never ran a real task through it, so no evidence exists either way. Nothing in mcgyvr's documentation may state it as established until the de-risk milestone is met.
